lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: Radius 6, central angle 60°. Arc and sector?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 67°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 154°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 5. From an external point 13 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 8, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
12, because the tangent bisects the radius
18, because the tangent extends beyond the circle
12, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 45°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 68°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 30°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 8. From an external point 17 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 90°, in terms of π.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
